name: ADUM3160BRWZ-RL
title: ADuM3160: full/low speed USB port isolator, 2.5 kV rms, 16-lead SOIC_W
summary: A digital isolator for the D+ and D- lines of an upstream-facing USB port, at low speed (1.5 Mbps) or full speed (12 Mbps), with the speed fixed by two strapping pins. It works out the direction of traffic packet by packet, carries J, K and SE0 across a transformer barrier, and holds the bus pull-up and pull-down resistors inside, so only series resistors and bypass capacitors are needed outside. Each side runs from a 4.5 V to 5.5 V bus voltage through its own internal 3.3 V regulator, or straight from 3.3 V. The barrier is rated 2500 V rms for 1 minute (UL 1577) in a 16-lead wide-body SOIC; W models are automotive qualified.

pins.name: VBUS1
pins.function: Side 1 supply. Wire it to the USB bus (4.5 V to 5.5 V); for a 3.3 V supply, join it to VDD1 and feed both from the 3.3 V rail. Needs a bypass capacitor to GND1.

pins.name: GND1
pins.function: Side 1 ground reference. Joined inside to pin 8; connect both pins to one ground.

pins.name: VDD1
pins.function: Side 1 3.3 V rail: the internal regulator's output when VBUS1 carries bus voltage (bypass it to GND1), or the 3.3 V supply input when joined to VBUS1. PDEN and SPU, when pulled high, connect to this pin.

pins.name: PDEN
pins.function: Pull-down enable, sampled as the part leaves reset. Tie to VDD1 in normal use. Held at GND1 at reset exit, it disconnects the downstream pull-down resistors so the buffer impedance can be measured.

pins.name: SPU
pins.function: Upstream buffer speed select, active high: high (to VDD1) picks full speed slew rate, timing and logic convention, low (to GND1) picks low speed. Must be strapped the same as SPD (pin 13).

pins.name: GND1
pins.function: Side 1 ground reference. Joined inside to pin 2; connect both pins to one ground.

pins.name: GND2
pins.function: Side 2 ground reference. Joined inside to pin 15; connect both pins to one ground.

pins.name: PIN
pins.function: Upstream pull-up enable: switches power to the upstream port's pull-up. Tie to VDD2 to attach at power-up, or drive it from a control signal to delay enumeration.

pins.name: SPD
pins.function: Downstream buffer speed select, active high: high (to VDD2) picks full speed, low (to GND2) picks low speed. Must be strapped the same as SPU (pin 5).

pins.name: VDD2
pins.function: Side 2 3.3 V rail: the internal regulator's output when VBUS2 carries bus voltage (bypass it to GND2), or the 3.3 V supply input when joined to VBUS2. SPD, when pulled high, may connect to this pin.

pins.name: GND2
pins.function: Side 2 ground reference. Joined inside to pin 9; connect both pins to one ground.

pins.name: VBUS2
pins.function: Side 2 supply. Wire it to a 4.5 V to 5.5 V bus; for a 3.3 V supply, join it to VDD2 and feed both from the 3.3 V rail. Needs a bypass capacitor to GND2.

circuits.title: Suggested PCB layout: bus-powered upstream, 3.3 V downstream
circuits.description: Side 1 takes 5 V from the USB bus on VBUS1, and its internal regulator puts 3.3 V out on VDD1; C1 decouples VBUS1 and C2 decouples VDD1, each to GND1. PDEN is tied to VDD1 for normal operation. Side 2 has no 5 V: VBUS2 and VDD2 are joined and fed from the peripheral's 3.3 V supply, which bypasses that side's regulator; C3 and C4 decouple the two pins to GND2. Each D line passes through a 24 Ω series resistor (R1 to R4) between its pin and the outside, which full speed needs and low speed does not. Both ground pins of each side are joined. SPU, SPD and PIN are brought out for strapping: SPU and SPD set to the same speed, PIN to VDD2 or a control line.

operation.text: The part watches both ports for activity. A transition out of idle on one side sets the direction, and data then flows that way until an end of packet or a long enough idle; the buffers are then turned off and both inputs watched again. While a packet passes, the receiving side keeps its own output buffers off and the driving side ignores edges on its inputs, so data cannot loop back through the barrier and latch it. Direction is decided afresh for every packet.

Timing follows the differential input transition; internal logic removes glitches that come from the different thresholds of the differential and single-ended receivers. Only the three valid states J, K and SE0 cross the barrier, so invalid SE0 and SE1 transients are not passed, and the output is rebuilt a fixed delay after the differential input.
There is no suspend mode: with the bus idle the upstream supply current (2.3 mA max) is under the 2.5 mA USB suspend limit.

An upstream-facing port has one speed, so slew rate, J/K levels and timing are strapped: SPU on side 1 and SPD on side 2, both high for full speed or both low for low speed. Unequal straps are not allowed and the host sees communication errors.

The bus pull-up and pull-down resistors are inside the part. PIN, on the downstream side, switches on the upstream idle-state pull-up, so the peripheral decides when the port attaches to the bus: tie PIN to VDD2 to attach at power-up, or to a 3.3 V logic signal to enumerate under control. Apart from this delayed pull-up the part is transparent to USB traffic.

The part sits in a peripheral's upstream-facing port. The host powers side 1 through the cable and UD+/UD- go to the cable; the peripheral's supply powers side 2 and DD+/DD- go to the peripheral's USB controller. Outside parts are only series resistors and bypass capacitors.

The added delay is comparable to one hub plus cable, so an isolated peripheral counts as though it had a hub inside when the depth of hubs in a chain is checked. A hub isolated at its upstream port by this part can be compliant when counted as two hub delays; the hub then lets the isolator run at full speed while low speed devices still work downstream of it.

Both ports meet USB cable-drive requirements, so the part can isolate a host port or a cable. Because its speed is fixed by pins, it cannot follow a peripheral's speed as a compliant downstream port must; such a port or cable works at one preset speed. That suits embedded hosts and custom cable assemblies, not general-purpose ports or cables.

Each side has an internal LDO regulator. With 4.5 V to 5.5 V on VBUSx, the regulator makes the 3.3 V that runs the D+/D- drivers, and VDDx brings it out for a bypass capacitor and for biasing pull-ups. With only 3.3 V available, feed it to both VBUSx and VDDx; the regulator is then disabled and the side runs straight from 3.3 V. The VBUS undervoltage lockout trips between 3.5 V and 4.35 V (side 1) or 4.4 V (side 2); the VDD lockout between 2.4 V and 3.1 V.
PDEN is read as the part comes out of reset. Tied to VDD1 the part works normally; at GND1 the downstream pull-down resistors are left disconnected so that buffer impedance can be measured.

If side 1 loses power, the downstream drivers go to high impedance within 32 bit times, and the downstream side always starts up in high impedance. If side 2 loses power, the upstream side removes its pull-up and turns its drivers off within 32 bit times. PIN low also presents a disconnected port.

For full speed every D line, on both sides, takes a 24 Ω ±1 % series resistor; low speed needs none. Bypass VBUSx and VDDx on each side with low-ESR capacitors of at least 0.1 µF, with no more than 10 mm of total lead length from the capacitor's two ends to the supply pin. Consider a capacitor between pins 2 and 8 and between pins 9 and 15 unless each side's two ground pins are joined close to the package. Logic signals are 3.3 V, taken from the local VDDx or a 3.3 V external source; the logic pins need no other interface parts.

Where large common-mode transients occur, keep coupling across the barrier on the board small, and lay out so that whatever coupling remains reaches every pin on one side alike; otherwise pin-to-pin differences on a side can exceed the absolute maximum ratings and cause latch-up or damage.

Each input edge sends a pulse of about 1 ns through the transformer to a bistable decoder. The pulses exceed 1.0 V and the decoder threshold is near 0.5 V, leaving a 0.5 V margin; an outside field is allowed to induce at most half of it, worked for the 3 V condition, which is the most sensitive. At 1 MHz the allowed field is 0.2 kgauss, inducing 0.25 V; a worst-case event during a pulse leaves 0.75 V, still above threshold. The same 1 MHz limit corresponds to 0.5 kA flowing 5 mm from the part. Strong high-frequency fields can still induce errors in loops formed by board traces, which the layout should avoid.

Insulation wears out under long voltage stress at a rate set by the waveform across it. Bipolar ac is the worst case, and its 50-year life sets the 560 V peak working voltage. Unipolar ac and dc stress the barrier far less, so 849 V peak is allowed for 50 years provided the voltage never crosses 0 V (it may stay on either side of zero, sine or not). Any other waveform is limited to the bipolar figure. The approved working voltages can exceed the 50-year voltage, and running there can shorten insulation life. Lifetimes come from accelerated testing above the rated voltage.
